## 1.1 A title that names the problem or the action

The game situation first, in two or three short sentences. Then the concept,
explained simply. A figure for every section:

![Caption as a full sentence.](images/name.png){#fig-name width=80%}

As @fig-name shows, …

::: {.callout-important title="Definition 1.1 — Term"}
A precise definition.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Example 1.1 — Short title"}
A worked example with numbered steps.

1. First step, with the numbers.
2. Second step.
3. The result in **bold**.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistake"}
The typical error and why it is wrong.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Short title"}
A 2–5 minute task the student does alone: on their phone, the lab computer,
a simulator of the lesson, a free tool or paper. Numbered steps. If Android
and iPhone (or Windows) differ, say how.

*Your result:* the concrete product (a number, a table, a file, a sketch, a
decision with one reason).
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="In game code"}
A short C# example to read (explain every code word).

```csharp
Vector3 position = new Vector3(1f, 2f, 4f);
```
:::

| Column | Column |
|---|---|
| value | value |
